input.initialPrompt:
You are a repository-rooted sub-session, opened per the BLOCKING GATE in Section 4.A.2 of this repository's AGENTS.md. Your working root is the repository you were launched in. Read AGENTS.md at the repo root before acting and follow it.

TASK: adopt the GitHub Actions workflow dependency lockfile and correct the master-text passages that declare it nonexistent or retired. Operator decision of 25/11/2026, tracked as LCV-719. This change already landed in 17 of the 22 fleet repositories; replicate it here. This repository is the 22nd, `lcv-leo/lcv-leo`: the operator explicitly ordered that it is part of the fleet.

STEP 1 - Branch. Verify `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, run `git fetch origin`, `entire status --json`. If the root is clean and on main, create `git checkout -b copilot/changelog-2026-11-lockfile origin/main`. If the root is NOT clean or NOT on main, STOP and report that instead of touching anything. Other agents work in this fleet concurrently: if `entire status --json` lists an active session on another branch in this checkout, report it and stop rather than sharing the checkout.

BASE FRESHNESS: other agents merge to main while you work. Immediately before committing, re-run `git fetch origin` and compare `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` with `git rev-parse origin/main`. If they differ, bring the branch current with `git merge --ff-only origin/main` (or rebase if you already committed) so the pull request diff contains only your change and not another agent's already-merged work. Report the base SHA you ended on.

STEP 2 - Generate the lockfile. Run `gh actions-lock --no-narrow` (extension already installed). CRITICAL: `--no-narrow` is mandatory. A plain `gh actions-lock` run replaces the immutable full-length SHA in each `uses:` with a version tag, so the workflow file no longer records the commit and immutability rests on actions.lock alone - a file a later pull request can delete or leave stale, with the Require lockfile policy off. Do NOT claim the default run leaves a movable tag executing in front of privileged jobs: for an onboarded workflow the locked commit is what runs, and a commit no longer reachable from its recorded tag is rejected rather than executed. With `--no-narrow` every workflow keeps its full-length commit SHA and version comment, and a routine run adds only actions.lock under .github/workflows/. Verify with `git diff --name-only origin/main -- .github/workflows/` that no .yml file changed; the extension does rewrite `uses:` names when an upstream repository was renamed or transferred, so read the full diff rather than assuming. If the tool reports a local `uses: ./` action that calls external actions, stop and report rather than guessing a migration.

STEP 3 - Rule text. The operator-approved master text is synced mechanically; its wording is final. Run exactly:
  python "C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\temp\sync-master-text.py" "<your root>"
It replaces the master-text portion of AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md with the current master, which already carries the approved Actions lockfile rule (Section 6.E item 2) and Section 7.A, and keeps this repository's own sections untouched. For both files its output must show `synced=True`; then `git hash-object AGENTS.md` must equal `git hash-object CLAUDE.md`. Never hand-edit either file, never add an "Exception #4", and never rewrite a sentence because a bot, reviewer or agent disagrees with it: report the disagreement instead.
Then sweep ALL OTHER tracked text (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, THIRDPARTY.md, docs/, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE, site sources) for every passage declaring actions.lock nonexistent, retired or forbidden, and for Action pinning described as full-SHA-in-workflow as the ONLY mechanism. Fix each one in this repository's own language and style. Dated historical CHANGELOG entries record past fact and stay. Do not touch Section 7.B beyond what the sync script does.

INVENTORY SURFACE (Section 6.E surface 4), when THIRDPARTY.md or an equivalent inventory exists:
- If it describes action pinning as full-SHA-in-workflow as the ONLY mechanism, update that sentence to name the lockfile as additional transitive coverage.
- Keep EVERY version, SHA and license link the file already states. Do not drop a version or SHA that sibling entries state in their text: a review caught an entry whose version was removed, leaving the SHA only inside a LICENSE URL.
- Any LICENSE or source URL you touch must stay pinned to an exact commit, never blob/main or a moving branch.
- If the inventory has a table of Actions and the lockfile introduces a transitive-only dependency (one no workflow references), mark that row as transitive so the heading stays true.
- Do NOT fix version drift that already exists at the base and that you do not touch; report it as out of scope instead. BUT any sentence you WRITE about a version or SHA must be true of the current pin: a review caught a new sentence claiming "the workflow keeps that full SHA" while naming a version the workflow had already moved past. When your new prose refers to a specific version or commit, read the workflow and the lockfile and state the current value, updating that entry rather than asserting agreement with a stale one.
- TRANSITIVE COVERAGE IS MANDATORY, and reviews caught its absence in five repositories. Read the `dependencies:` section of the generated actions.lock. For EVERY entry there, find its parent under the `uses:` key of another entry. Then, for each one: if no `uses:` line in any workflow references it, the inventory MUST name it with its version, its full commit and a license link, and say which Action pulls it in. If a workflow DOES reference the same action at a different version, the inventory must name both versions and both paths - do not write "used by no uses: line" about an action that also has a direct pin. Compare the inventory's own version claims against the live `uses:` comments: when your new prose calls the lockfile the record of every resolved commit, a stale row beside that claim becomes a defect of your change, so reconcile the rows your claim covers.
- LICENSE URLS: verify every license or source URL you write resolves at the commit you name (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/LICENSE?ref=<sha>`). Never substitute blob/main for a pinned commit in an entry that pins one, and never invent a version - read it from the lockfile's `ref:` field.

CONSISTENCY CHECKS a review has already caught, run each one and report its result:
1. GENERATOR FLAG: every sentence you write or edit that instructs how to generate or refresh the lockfile MUST name `gh actions-lock --no-narrow`, never a bare `gh actions-lock`. A bare mention points readers at the invocation the rule forbids. Grep every changed Markdown file for `gh actions-lock` and classify each hit: an instruction must carry `--no-narrow`; naming the CLI extension ("the `gh actions-lock` CLI extension") or describing the forbidden plain run is legitimate. Report the classification, not just a count.
2. NO REMAINING PROHIBITION: after editing, grep ALL tracked Markdown (root, docs/, .github/, templates, public legal copies) for every passage still declaring actions.lock nonexistent, retired or forbidden. Report each remaining hit and why it is legitimate (a dated historical CHANGELOG entry) or fix it. A prior review found the third prohibition in CONTRIBUTING.md in one repository and in a README governance paragraph in another - do not assume it lives in a "Workspace Policy" paragraph.
3. NO DUPLICATED TEXT: when replacing a sentence inside a long bullet, replace ONLY that sentence, never the whole bullet. A prior attempt appended the entire bullet after its own trailing sentence, duplicating the paragraph. Verify the bullet's key phrase occurs exactly once per file.
4. MIRROR PARITY: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md must be byte-identical; compare SHA-256 hashes and report the result.
5. FORMATTER STYLE: match the repository's own Markdown emphasis convention. One repository's Prettier normalizes emphasis to underscores, and asterisks failed CI. If the repo has a prettier config or a format gate covering Markdown, run it on the files you changed.
6. NO DRIVE-BY: every changed line must serve the lockfile adoption. Do not add a .gitignore or .prettierignore entry for an unrelated local artifact, do not reformat untouched prose, do not fix an unrelated bug. A review rejected an ignore entry for a file whose source was unknown; report such an artifact instead of hiding it.
7. SECTION REFERENCES RESOLVE: any sentence you write that cites "Section X" must name the document that contains it, because THIRDPARTY.md and its public legal copies are read outside the repository. Write "AGENTS.md, Section 6.E item 2" or state the rule directly - never a bare section number.
8. PUBLISHED COPIES: if the repository publishes a copy of an inventory or policy (for example public/legal/THIRDPARTY.md or src/legal/), update every copy of the text you changed and verify byte-identity by hash. Report which copies exist and which you touched.
9. RULE CONTRADICTIONS: read the sentence you wrote as a whole. A review caught "adds or edits actions.lock only, and still sweeps all eight surfaces" reading as a contradiction; separate what the tool touches from what the author must still check.

Add one entry to the CHANGELOG.md Unreleased section recording the adoption, in this repository's own language and style, referencing LCV-719.

STEP 4 - Run EVERY local gate this repository defines, before any push. Read package.json scripts (root and every sub-package) and .github/workflows/ci.yml to find the exact commands CI runs, and run those. Set TMP/TEMP/TMPDIR to a temp/ folder inside this repository first; never use the system temp. If CI generates types before validating (for example `npm run types`), do the same.

A composite `check` script often chains format, lint, typecheck and tests: run the composite AND report which sub-gate failed if it exits non-zero, rather than reporting only the composite result. Run the formatter over the files you changed, not only over the repository's default glob: a prior push failed CI because a Markdown table edit broke Prettier while the local run had only covered HTML.

When a gate exits non-zero, classify it before proceeding: (i) caused by your diff - fix it; (ii) pre-existing at the base - prove it by stashing your changes and re-running, and report it as out of scope; (iii) environmental, such as a dependency missing from a pre-existing node_modules or a Git-ignored local file absent from CI - prove which, and record it as a validation gap. Never report a gate as passed when it did not run or did not pass.

Also run `gh actions-lock --verify` and zizmor (use `.github/zizmor.yml` as config only if that file exists; the local zizmor version may differ from the CI Action's pinned version - report both).

STEP 5 - Commit with `git commit -S -F temp/commit-msg.txt`, Conventional Commits, message in a file. Include the trailer `Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>`. Because you run inside this repository root, Entire's hooks capture your session and add the Entire-Checkpoint trailer automatically - verify with `git log -1 --format=%B` and confirm the id exists as a local ref via `git for-each-ref "refs/entire/checkpoints/**" | Select-String <id>`. Do NOT run `entire session attach`: using it here is what produced an orphan checkpoint in an earlier attempt.

STEP 6 - STOP before pushing. Do not push, do not open a pull request. Report: branch name, commit SHA, the Entire-Checkpoint id and whether its ref exists locally, the full list of changed files, every gate with its exit code, and any validation gap. The parent session runs the separate adversarial review and the push.

Constraints: never pass --no-verify to git. Never edit files outside this repository. Keep every temporary file in this repository's temp/. Do not install dependencies unless a gate fails because they are missing.
REPOSITORY NOTES for lcv-leo/lcv-leo:
- It is a public user-account repository (owner `lcv-leo`), not an organization repository: pass `--repo lcv-leo/lcv-leo` to every gh command that needs a repository.
- 8 workflows, 21 external `uses:` lines, all full-SHA with version comments; `.github/dependabot.yml` exists.
- The lockfile will add three transitive dependencies: `oven-sh/setup-bun` (inside anthropics/claude-code-action), a second revision of `actions/upload-artifact` (inside actions/upload-pages-artifact) and a second revision of `github/codeql-action` (inside zizmorcore/zizmor-action). Name each one in the inventory as step "INVENTORY SURFACE" requires, with the commit the lockfile records and a license link at that commit.
- `gh pr list`/`gh pr view` examples that use the organization are not needed: stop before the push.

<sql>
**Session database**: persists for this session and is isolated from other sessions. Use it for structured operational data such as todos, test cases, batches, and state.

**Built-in tables:**
- `todos`: id, title, description, status (pending/in_progress/done/blocked), created_at, updated_at
- `todo_deps`: todo_id, depends_on

`todos` and `todo_deps` already exist—insert into them; never create them.

**Todo tracking with dependencies:** Use descriptive kebab-case IDs, gerund titles (for example "Creating user auth module"), and self-contained descriptions. Status meanings:
- `pending`: not started
- `in_progress`: active; set before starting
- `done`: complete
- `blocked`: cannot proceed; explain why in the description

Record every actual prerequisite in `todo_deps`; do not infer dependencies from list order. Before inserting a dependency, insert both todos referenced by its `todo_deps` row. Todos with no prerequisites should remain independent.

Example with two dependent todos, one independent todo, and a ready-todo query:
```sql
-- Todo dependency example
INSERT INTO todos (id, title, description) VALUES
  ('user-model', 'Creating user model', 'Define the User schema and relations in src/models/user.ts'),
  ('api-routes', 'Creating API routes', 'Implement routes that use the User model'),
  ('theme-toggle', 'Adding theme toggle', 'Add an independent dark-mode toggle to the settings page');
INSERT INTO todo_deps (todo_id, depends_on) VALUES ('api-routes', 'user-model');
SELECT t.* FROM todos t
WHERE t.status = 'pending'
AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM todo_deps td
    JOIN todos dep ON td.depends_on = dep.id
    WHERE td.todo_id = t.id AND dep.status != 'done'
);
```

Create other tables as needed to load/query data (including CSVs, API responses, and file listings), store structured intermediate results, or manage workflows. Example session state:
```sql
CREATE TABLE session_state (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT);
INSERT OR REPLACE INTO session_state (key, value) VALUES ('current_phase', 'testing');
SELECT value FROM session_state WHERE key = 'current_phase';
```
</sql>

## 4. Mandatory Operational Protocol: Entire + GitHub Enterprise Integration & Anti-Hang PR Flow (`LCV-517` / Ruleset ID `20582436`)

GitHub Enterprise and Entire run in parallel. Entire's architecture ([Entire docs](https://docs.entire.com/)) and the `LCV-517` sequence below are mandatory for full session and checkpoint capture and to keep Pull Requests from hanging on the Enterprise Rulesets ([rulesets](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets); `20582436` on `main`, `20613778` on every other branch).

### A. Entire Architecture, Hook Locations, Session Spawning, Crosslinking & Handoff

Entire captures agent sessions through repository-level agent hooks and links them to commits with the `Entire-Checkpoint` and `Entire-Attribution` trailers, stored under `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` or `entire/checkpoints/v1`.

1. **Hook configuration per agent, present before the session starts** (installed with `entire agent add <agent>` by the operator or on the operator's order, as the Cursor hooks were; agents never change hook configuration on their own): Antigravity CLI `.agents/hooks.json` plus the global title-feed wrapper in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` (`entire hooks antigravity title-tee`); Claude Code `.claude/settings.json`; Codex `.codex/hooks.json`; Copilot CLI `.github/hooks/entire.json`; Cursor `.cursor/hooks.json` (operator decision, [Cursor hooks](https://cursor.com/docs/hooks)); external agents `"external_agents": true` in `.entire/settings.local.json`, honored only while that file is untracked (`entire agent-help session attach`). Running agent processes do not load hooks added after they started, and hooks capture only sessions that run inside the Git repository or worktree root where Entire is enabled.

2. **The `lcv-workspace` parent-folder problem.** The operator opens the IDEs at `C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\`, outside any repository root, where Entire's hooks capture nothing.

   > **BLOCKING GATE — Repository-Rooted Sub-Session (operator decision):** before editing any file, staging, or committing in a repository, the agent runs in a session whose working root is that repository's root or that worktree's root. A session started anywhere else opens a sub-session inside that root (commands below) and does the repository work there. The only alternative is Entire's native linking (`entire session adopt` from another worktree, or `entire session attach`, below), only when opening the sub-session is technically impossible, with the raw error recorded as proof. If neither is possible, stop: do not edit, commit, push, or open a Pull Request, and report the proof. Work done in violation of this gate is not delivered work. A sub-session runs the checkout's tracked hooks and configuration at startup, so never open one in a checkout of a branch not created by the operator or the agent (Section 3); review such a branch read-only from the agent's own checkout.

   Binding procedure:
   * Change the working directory to the exact repository root (`C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\<repo>`) or worktree (`C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\.worktrees\<worktree>`), strip inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, and `GIT_COMMON_DIR` ([git environment](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Environment-Variables)), and verify with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` ([git rev-parse](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rev-parse)).
   * Run `entire status --json` and `entire agent list`. If the agent's hooks are missing or stale, run `entire doctor` for the diagnosis (its offer to fix is declined because the agent's shell is non-interactive) and ask the operator to run `entire agent add <agent> --force`. In a fresh worktree, confirm that the directory named by `git config core.hooksPath` exists (for example `.husky/_`, Git-ignored and created by the repository's install step); without it no hook fires ([githooks](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks)).
   * Spawn the repository-rooted session in that directory: Codex `codex exec "<task>"` or `codex -C <dir> exec "<task>"` ([Codex CLI](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands?surface=cli)); Claude Code `claude -p "<task>" --strict-mcp-config` (never `--bare`, which skips hooks; launch subagents so Entire rolls them into the parent checkpoint) ([Claude Code headless mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless)); GitHub Copilot CLI `copilot -p "<task>" --allow-all --disallow-temp-dir` or `copilot -C <dir> -p "<task>" --allow-all --disallow-temp-dir` (operator decision: a `-p` run denies a tool request that would prompt and, in an untrusted folder, skips the repository hooks; subfolders of a trusted folder are trusted, `copilot help permissions`), or `entire session resume <BRANCH>` / `copilot --resume <SESSION_ID>` ([Copilot CLI programmatic use](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/automate-copilot-cli/run-cli-programmatically), [Entire: Copilot CLI](https://docs.entire.com/agents/copilot-cli)); Cursor: open the repository or worktree itself as the workspace folder; Antigravity `agy` in that directory, or `entire session resume <BRANCH>` / `agy --conversation <SESSION_ID>` ([Antigravity docs](https://antigravity.google/docs)); Antigravity subagent hooks are not attached automatically, so Antigravity work runs in the repo-rooted `agy` session or is linked with `entire session adopt`/`attach` before pushing.
   * **Session identity:** trust `entire session current --json` only when `resolution` is `caller-env` or `ancestry`; `other-worktree` can be any session of the shared store (`entire agent-help session current`).
   * **Adoption (`entire session adopt`):** a session that started in another worktree of the same repository (a worktree that already tracks it; a session started in `lcv-workspace` is not tracked anywhere and uses the crosslinking bullet instead) and continued into the target is adopted before committing: `entire status --json`, then `entire session adopt <SESSION_ID> --from <SOURCE_PATH> --yes` (between worktrees of the same repository, which share one session store, the command requires `--yes` or `--force`, `entire agent-help session adopt`); the next `git commit -S` links it.

   * **Handoff (`session-handoff` protocol):** when continuing another agent's or session's work, run `entire session current --json` and `entire session list --json`, stream the transcript with `entire session info <id> --transcript`, write the structured handoff (*Task Overview, Current State, Important Discoveries, Next Steps, Context to Preserve, Unanswered Question*), and resume. If `resolution` is neither `caller-env` nor `ancestry`, report the value, do not resume from that session id, and choose the session by its id from `entire session list --json`.

### B. Inviolable Rules of `LCV-517` (Ruleset ID `20582436`)

1. **SSH commit signing:** every commit created locally (`commit`, `amend`, `merge`) is signed with SSH (`git commit -S`, `gpg.format=ssh`, 1Password SSH signer, [1Password Git commit signing](https://www.1password.dev/ssh/git-commit-signing)); never GPG/OpenPGP for your own commits, and never create commits or pull requests through the API from a local session (commits with `git`, pull requests with `gh pr create`, Section 4.C). Unsigned commits fail `required_signatures` ([rules API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules)). The squash commit on `main` is created and signed by GitHub itself (`web-flow`, GitHub's OpenPGP key): that signature is GitHub's, not the operator's, and never a violation of this rule; verify it through the API, `verification.verified == true` ([commits API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/commits), [signature verification](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/about-commit-signature-verification)). `git config user.email` matches the operator's verified GitHub email so `entire.com` never shows `"Unknown author"`.
2. **Conventional Commits** for every message ([Conventional Commits 1.0.0](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/)).
3. **Temporary artifact isolation:** every temporary file stays in `temp/` and is deleted before completion (Section 3).
4. **Entire hooks are never bypassed:** Entire works through `prepare-commit-msg`, `commit-msg`, `post-commit`, `post-rewrite`, and `pre-push` ([githooks](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks)). Never pass `--no-verify` to any `git` command (`-n` in `git commit`; [git commit](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit), [git push](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-push)).

### C. Canonical 5-Step Execution & Anti-Hang PR Flow (Exact Certified Order)

Whenever implementing changes and taking a Pull Request to merge, execute these five steps in this order:

* **Step 1: Branch & Development (inside the repository or worktree root)**
  1. Confirm the root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, run `git fetch origin` ([git fetch](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-fetch)), and verify capture with `entire status --json`.
  2. **Branch in the root or worktree (operator decision):** evaluate and state the choice and its reason; never apply one by default. A branch in the root only when the root checkout is clean (`git status --porcelain` empty), on `main`, and not in use by another session or front; preferred for one sequential change and when the repository depends on Git-ignored artifacts of the root (`admin-app`, hooks in `.husky/_`). A worktree when the root has uncommitted work, is in use by another session, must stay on `main` for a live process, or when several changes proceed in parallel; a new worktree contains only tracked files, so confirm its hooks and install artifacts first ([git worktree](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree)).
  3. Branch name `<agent>/<task>` with `<agent>` one of `claude`, `codex`, `agy`, `copilot`, `cursor`; Ruleset `20613778` accepts only its live `branch_name_pattern` (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/rulesets/20613778`, [rulesets API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules)). Exactly one of: `git checkout -b <agent>/<task> origin/main` in the root ([git checkout](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-checkout)), or `git worktree add C:/Users/lcvle/lcv-workspace/.worktrees/<repo>-<task> -b <agent>/<task> origin/main` followed by the repository-rooted sub-session inside it (Section 4.A.2), from which Step 1.4 through Step 5.3 run.
  4. Implement and validate locally on the project stack in PowerShell, never Git Bash, with every temporary output in `temp/`; a dependency version change is validated by CI instead (Section 3).

* **Step 2: SSH-Signed Commit & Checkpoint Linking**
  1. `git add <files>` (never `temp/`) ([git add](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-add)).
  2. `git commit -S -F temp/commit-msg.txt` — the message in a file, because messages contain backticks ([git commit](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit)).
  3. Confirm the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer with `git log -1 --show-signature --format=fuller` and `entire checkpoint list --json`. If the session was captured (`entire status --json`) but not linked, run `entire session attach <SESSION_ID> --agent <AGENT> --commit <FULL_SHA>` without `--force` first, show its plan to the operator, and rerun with `--force` only after the operator agrees; if `attach` amended the commit, verify that the SSH signature on `HEAD` is still valid.
  4. **Adversarial review before the push (operator decision):** after the commit and before every push that changes content, write `temp/pr-body.md`; a separate reviewer session, spawned in the checkout with the Section 4.A.2 commands, runs the Section 8.B prompts on its review context. Fix each finding in a new signed commit, or disprove it with code evidence or an operator directive in this text and record the disproof in the task's Linear Issue, until a round leaves no finding open; a finding open after three rounds goes to the operator.

* **Step 3: Publication & Pull Request Creation**
  1. `git push -u origin <branch>` (the `pre-push` hook syncs `refs/entire/checkpoints/*`).
  2. `gh pr create --title "<type>(<scope>): <description>" --body-file temp/pr-body.md` ([gh pr create](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_create)).
  3. **Ready for review only, never draft (operator decision):** never `--draft`, never `gh pr ready --undo`, never convert between draft and ready. Each conversion emits the `ready_for_review` or `converted_to_draft` activity of the `pull_request` event, which reruns every workflow subscribed to it and restarts the review bots ([events that trigger workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#pull_request), [gh pr ready](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_ready)); on `astrologo-android` the gates take about one hour, so a draft opened, made ready, and drafted again runs them three times.

* **Step 4: Anti-Hang Handshake (`LCV-517`, mandatory right after `gh pr create`)**
  Run `git commit --amend --no-edit -S` and `git push --force-with-lease origin <branch>` ([git push](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-push)). Reason recorded in `LCV-517` (observed behavior, not described in GitHub's documentation): Secret Scanning stays pending (`"Waiting for secret scan to complete..."`) when the first commit was pushed before the Pull Request existed; the amend and force push after creation emit `pull_request.synchronize`, which completes Secret Scanning and triggers CodeQL and Code Quality. Entire keeps the checkpoint link across the amend through `post-rewrite`. Verify with `git ls-remote origin "refs/entire/checkpoints/*" | Select-String -SimpleMatch "<CHECKPOINT_ID>"` ([git ls-remote](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-ls-remote)) in the ref-based layout, or `entire checkpoint list --json` in the `entire/checkpoints/v1` layout, and `git log -1 --show-signature`. The head left by the handshake is the first head under review; from then on Section 5.G, item 4, applies.

* **Step 5: Findings, CI, Merge & Cleanup**
  1. After every push, `gh pr checks <pr> --watch` ([gh pr checks](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_checks)) and `entire trail finding list <repo>/<trail> --freshness any --json` inside the repository checkout (add `--project gh/<project>` only when the project is not origin's owner; 100 per page, continue with `--cursor`; `entire agent-help trail finding list`). Fix real defects and findings, resolve them with `entire trail finding resolve <id> -m "fixed in <sha>"`, and re-verify.

     > **BLOCKING GATE — Active Watch and Zero Open Findings (operator decision):** from the moment a Pull Request or Trail exists until it is merged, keep watching it; bots and the Entire review can post minutes after the checks finish, and every push starts a new round. After each push and again immediately before merging, inventory: review threads, resolved and unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads`, every page, [pull request review threads](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/pulls#object-pullrequestreviewthread)); every review body with its suppressed comments ([reviews API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews)); the conversation comments ([issue comments API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/comments)); Entire Trail findings (`--freshness any`); open diff threads of the linked Linear review; failed or pending checks and code scanning alerts on the head ([code scanning alerts API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning)). **While any finding is open, the Pull Request or Trail is not merged or approved**, whatever the merge button allows. A finding closes only when its code was fixed and the thread or finding is resolved citing the fixing commit, or when it is disproved with evidence from the code or an operator directive in this text and resolved citing that evidence.
  2. `gh pr view <pr> --json mergeStateStatus` ([gh pr view](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_view)).
  3. **The operator merges, or orders the agent to merge (operator decision);** without that order, hand the operator the pull request with every gate clear and the squash body file below. When ordered: GitHub builds the squash message from `squash_merge_commit_message` (`COMMIT_MESSAGES` on the fleet, `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo> --jq .squash_merge_commit_message`), and any `--body` replaces it entirely, observed behavior not described in GitHub's documentation (`admin-app` #810 reached `main` without its `Entire-Checkpoint:` lines; [squash commit message](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/configuring-commit-squashing-for-pull-requests), [repositories API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/repos)).   4. After the API shows the Pull Request `MERGED`: in the root, `git checkout main && git pull --ff-only origin main` ([git pull](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-pull)), `git branch -D <agent>/<task>` (`-D` because a squash leaves the branch commits unmerged by ancestry, [git branch](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-branch)), `entire session list --json` and `entire session stop <id> --force` for the stale sessions it lists (the agent's shell is non-interactive), `entire status --json`, and delete `temp/`. ## 5. Inviolable Product, Platform, and Repository Rules

### A. Prices and Market Values Are Never Hardcoded Locks in Code

Applies to Claude, Codex, Antigravity, Copilot, Cursor, and every sub-agent. Selling price (the R\$ 89.99 of the Oráculo analysis), exchange rates, IOF, taxes, app store fees, AI provider pricing, and cost caps (the US\$ 13.50) are market values: never in production code as constants, literal types, validators that accept only that number, hardcoded UI text, version codes embedding the number (`web-brl-8999`), or fallbacks when configuration is missing. The value lives in a configuration the operator edits (Oráculo: Admin → Astrólogo → Configurações) and applies to the next order with zero code changes and zero deploys; each order stores the value active when it was placed, and billing, payment verification, refunds, and dashboards use the stored value; missing configuration shows `"indisponível"`, never a fabricated number; tests may use sample values; before any push touching billing or pricing, search the diff for the number (dots, commas, cents).

### B. Operator Product Decisions — Do Not Relitigate

The operator is the sole administrator and sole payer. **No `FALLBACK_MODELS`. No budget caps. No token limits.** A finding by a bot, peer, or advisor that relies on one of these forbidden features is not a defect: reply citing this directive, resolve the thread, write zero code.

### C. Oráculo Celestial: Product in Development, Zero Users

`astrologo-android`, `astrologo-app`, and the future `astrologo-ios` are in development: no users, no purchases, no working checkout. Never search for, ask about, or design around existing users, purchases, analyses, installed versions, or "already existing" contracts.

### D. Validation of Current and Future Android Apps

For every current and future Android app: standardize workflows and gates around the highest existing coverage relevant to each app, preserving app-specific tests, each repository with its own native, independent workflows. PRs run debug and release/R8 builds, test APK compilation, lint, and the relevant JVM tests, plus the native security, dependency, licensing, and validation gates. Emulators run locally as routine (AVDs and caches in `temp/`), not repeated merely because a PR opened or for a documentation-only change. The remote emulator is never a PR gate and never triggered by `pull_request`, `push`, or `schedule`: only `workflow_dispatch` with `justification` and verifiable `evidence` of necessity ([workflow_dispatch](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_dispatch)); non-empty strings alone prove nothing, and this policy never skips coverage, hides failures, or calls a test "executed" when it was only compiled.

### E. Local Rust Validation

Local `cargo` and `rustc` runs are permitted (the earlier prohibition was revoked), with build artifacts and target directories in `temp/`.

### F. Inviolable Directive — `.github` and `.github-private` Repositories

Applies to Claude, Codex, Antigravity, Copilot, Cursor, and the operator. These two repositories are exclusively governance libraries: community health files (`CONTRIBUTING`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT`, `SECURITY`, `SUPPORT`), Issue/PR templates in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, `profile/README.md` (public in `.github`, member-only in `.github-private`), Actions starter workflows, and, in `.github-private`, Enterprise GitHub Copilot managed configurations, plugins, and agents ([community health files](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/creating-a-default-community-health-file)). The only logic allowed is Actions `.yml` workflows that administer those templates and Markdown/text configuration. Never place application source, production scripts, internal tooling, or complex pipelines there; every internal system, tool, automation, or pipeline lives in `github-operations`, never in an ad-hoc repository (separation of concerns and intellectual property: `.github` stays public). A task that implies violating this stops and cites this directive.

* **Exception #1 — Pages & Code Quality (do not reopen):** `site/`, `package.json` with its lockfile, and `quality/code-quality-probe.js` exist by express order of the operator to support GitHub Pages and enable Code Quality; never an audit finding, never proposed for removal.

## 6. Zero-Tolerance Anti-Slop Engineering Protocol, Contract Surface Sweeps & 5-Stage Gatekeeper

"Slop" is avoidable, low-trust work caused by not understanding the repository well enough: unverified assumptions, lazy truncation, hallucinated interfaces, duplicate systems, type evasion and catch-all masking, premature abstraction, unrequested mutation, iteration debris, filler. Any violation below is a critical execution failure.

### A. Anti-Truncation & Complete Implementation
No placeholders, truncation markers, or elisions (`// TODO`, `// FIXME`, `// implement logic here`, `// ... rest of the code`, `/* existing code */`, `pass`). Every code block, script, or patch is complete, syntactically valid, fully imported, and immediately runnable. Never delegate mechanical work to the operator ("repeat this pattern", "add the imports").

### B. Epistemic Anti-Slop
Read the exact live state of a file, function, schema, or workflow and its nearby helpers and tests before writing or referencing it; reuse the repository's established pattern instead of a parallel helper or ad-hoc parser. Never guess library methods, CLI flags, GraphQL fields, environment variables, or SDK signatures: verify against the installed lockfile versions and the official documentation. Never hand-edit or regex a lockfile (`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `Cargo.lock`); regenerate only with the official tool, in the modes of Section 3.

### C. Architectural, Sequencing & Code Anti-Slop
Strict typing (`strict: true` in TypeScript, strict Python 3.10+ annotations, explicit Go/Rust types); never `any`, `as unknown as T`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `# type: ignore`, or loose `Record<string, any>`: fix the contract. No empty `catch {}`, no log-and-continue that corrupts state, no silent fallbacks (`|| "default"`, `?? 0`) for missing business configuration, credentials, or market prices: fail fast with structured, secret-free logging. No inconsistent, orphaned, or lost state when a later step fails; no irreversible write before a fallible call; cleanup on success and failure; tests use isolated directories or repositories inside `temp/` and never touch the operator's real config, keychain, or checkout. No speculative abstractions, single-implementation interfaces, wrapper classes, or heavy patterns for linear problems: flat, readable, immutable, pure, modular code (SRP, DRY). No accidental $O(N^2)$ loops, N+1 queries, unindexed lookups, unbounded accumulations, or unclosed handles.

### D. Diff Hygiene & Non-Destructive Editing
Modify only the lines and files the task requires; no drive-by refactors, renames, or formatting sweeps; zero iteration debris (dead code, stale comments, unused helpers, abandoned approaches, debug logs). Delete no high-value architectural comment; add no comment that restates the next line, narrates the diff, or explains what the conventions make obvious; comment only the *why* of a non-obvious invariant, security boundary, or business constraint. Preserve encodings and line endings (`core.autocrlf=false`, [git config](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config)); never apply blind global regex replacements to prose or manifests.

### E. Pinned Dependency Bump = 8-Point Contract Surface Sweep

Changing the version of a GitHub Action or pinned dependency is never two files. Follow the `bump-dependencia-pinada` skill (`C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\.claude\skills\bump-dependencia-pinada\SKILL.md`) and sweep all eight surfaces:

2. **Lockfiles:** as Section 6.B requires. There is no GitHub Actions lockfile (operator decision); full-SHA pinning is enforced natively by `sha_pinning_required` ([Actions permissions API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/permissions)). A Wrangler update also regenerates `worker-configuration.d.ts` under the Section 3 exception and commits it before pushing.
3. **Repository Actions allowlist:** may pin the exact commit SHA; inspect repository by repository and admit the new commit alongside the old one before merging ([allowed actions](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/permissions#set-allowed-actions-and-reusable-workflows-for-a-repository)).

Before delivering code or releasing a Pull Request, pass all five stages with concrete proof: (1) principal architectural review (flaws, coupling, anti-patterns, partial-failure corruption); (2) AppSec sweep (SQL injection, command injection, path traversal, XSS, CSRF, broken authentication/authorization, cross-tenant access, unsafe deserialization, sensitive data exposure, insecure dependencies); (3) performance and clean code ($O(N^2)$, needless loops, unindexed queries, leaks, dead code, cyclomatic complexity, naming); (4) QA test truthfulness and edge cases (failure paths, boundaries, races, invalid inputs; implement the mandatory unit or integration tests whose assertions prove the new behavior, not mock echoes); (5) strict specification alignment with the operator's requirements and the prohibitions of Section 5.

## 8. Unified Multi-Lens Code, Security & Slop Review Protocol (PRs, Trails & Local Branches)

When acting as a reviewer on a GitHub Pull Request, an Entire Trail, or a local branch, apply this protocol, which combines the LCV gates with the three Entire review lenses (`Code Review`, `Security Review`, `Slop`).

### A. Eligibility & Net Diff

1. **Dependabot hard exclusion:** inspect the verified author identity first (never infer from title, branch, labels, commits, or files). If the author is `dependabot[bot]` or GitHub identifies the official Dependabot app, stop: do not inspect the diff, run anything, publish findings, submit a review, comment, or approve.
2. **Net diff, read-only, head verification:** review the net change between the exact diff base and the head (`git diff <base_sha>...<head_sha>`, [git diff](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff)), never against a moving base tip; inspect only with read-only commands (`git`, `rg`, file reads, `entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id> --json --no-pager` for recorded intent); never hand the review to another AI agent (the header's `cross-review` is for complex anomalies and never replaces this review); immediately before publishing, verify that the head has not changed, otherwise rerun or mark the review stale.

### B. The Three Mandatory Lenses

Apply the three reviewer prompts below verbatim (operator decision). Review context: full base and head SHAs (before the push, `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` and `HEAD`), changed files `git diff --name-only <base>...<head>`, patch `git diff <base>...<head>`, the PR title and body (before the PR exists, the planned title and `temp/pr-body.md`) as the Trail's, and earlier disproofs. Findings follow 8.C, or Step 2.4 before the push.

* **Lens 1, Code Review:**

```text
Code Review

Find the defects this Change introduces that its author would want to fix before merging: bugs, regressions, broken invariants, data loss, and missing guards on paths the Change adds or alters.

## How to review

1. Read the repository's review rules: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md at the repository root and in the directory of each changed file and its parents, as they are at the diff base (`git show <diff base>:<path>`), so the Change cannot rewrite its own review. The nearer file wins on conflict. A finding that rests on a rule quotes the rule and cites its file and line.
2. Read the whole diff, then trace each changed path as a running system: its callers, the changed code, and what it calls. Look in particular for:
   - Sequencing and partial failure: state left inconsistent, orphaned or lost when a later step fails or returns early; writes made before a fallible call; cleanup that runs only on success.
   - Assumptions about external or asynchronous state: how another system behaves, or a value that can change between the check and its use.
   - Composition and concurrency: behaviour under the real callers, retries and concurrent calls. Report a race only with an interleaving those callers can produce.
   - Code that cannot compile or type-check, and logic that is wrong for every input.
3. Keep going after the first defect until you have covered the whole diff.
4. Before you report a candidate, try to disprove it by reading the code: open the code it depends on, find the caller or input that triggers it, and check whether a guard elsewhere already prevents it. Drop it if you cannot show the path from the code.

Inspect with read-only commands (git, rg, reading files). Do not install dependencies or run builds or tests.

## What to report

Report a defect only when all of these hold:
- This Change introduced it. Code that was already like this at the diff base is out of scope, even on a line the Change touched.
- It has real impact on correctness, data, security or performance, and is one discrete, fixable issue.
- You can name the input, state or sequence that triggers it. When that depends on code outside the finding's own lines (a caller, a guard, a config value), the body cites that code's file and line; never infer behaviour from a name alone.
- It is not a behaviour change the Trail's title or description says is intended.
- Fixing it asks no more rigor than the surrounding code holds itself to, and the author would fix it if they knew.

Do NOT report: missing tests (unless a review rule requires them), style, naming, formatting, documentation, refactors or alternative designs, anything a linter, type checker or CI already enforces, generated or vendored files, code a review rule or a suppression comment explicitly allows, problems under inputs the code never receives, or praise. Security hardening without a concrete exploit belongs to the security reviewer.

## How to write findings

- One finding per distinct defect. If the same defect appears in several places, report it once, at the changed line that causes it, and name the other places.
- Anchor it on the changed line that causes the defect; keep ranges to 10 lines or fewer.
- Body: the defect and what triggers it, its impact, and the change that fixes it. One short paragraph, at most 3 lines of code, matter-of-fact.
- Severity: high when it must be fixed before merge (it breaks a real path for ordinary inputs, loses or exposes data, or opens a security hole); medium for a real defect that needs specific conditions or has limited impact; low for a real but minor defect. Never overstate it.
- Confidence: 0.9 or more when you traced the triggering path in the code; 0.7 to 0.9 with strong evidence and one assumption left; 0.5 to 0.7 when one condition could not be confirmed. Do not report anything below 0.5.
- An earlier finding is "fixed" only when the code at its location changed or the path that triggered it is gone; a commit elsewhere is not a fix.

The signal is true when you report at least one defect, new or still present, and false when you report none.
```

* **Lens 2, Security Review:**

```text
Security Review

Review this change for security vulnerabilities it introduces or exposes: missing or bypassable authentication and authorization checks, privilege escalation and cross-tenant access; injection (SQL, shell command, path traversal, template); unsafe deserialization; secrets or credentials in code, logs or errors; insecure defaults; missing validation of untrusted input at a trust boundary; and exposure of data to callers who should not see it.

Trace untrusted input from where it enters to where it is used. Report only issues with a plausible exploit path through the changed code, and state the impact.

Do NOT report: general code quality, style, missing tests, or hardening suggestions without a concrete vulnerability.

The signal is true when you report at least one vulnerability, false when you report none.
```

* **Lens 3, Slop:**

```text
Slop

You are a very strict reviewer of agent-generated code slop. Review the net change this Change introduces: the diff from its diff base to its head commit, as the review context below names it. Judge the code, not who wrote it.

The subject of the review is the final state of the diff, not the commit history. Ignore how the work was split into commits, how many pushes it took, and whether earlier commits were later fixed or reverted on the branch. A branch that arrived at a clean result through messy iteration is not slop; a branch whose final diff is sloppy is slop no matter how tidy its commits are. Anything already at the diff base is existing code, not the subject of the review.

Work from the review context:

1. Start with the changed files and the patch in the review context. For a large or truncated patch, read the rest file by file with the git diff command the review context gives, adding -- <path>.
2. Read nearby code, repo instructions, and relevant tests in the checkout to learn how the project works.
3. You may skim the commit log from the diff base to the head commit to understand intent, but do not grade individual commits.

Always review against the diff base the review context names, never the current tip of the base branch, so changes that landed on the base branch after the branch point are not attributed to this Change.

This review is read-only against the repo's own tooling. Do not install dependencies and do not run the project's build, typecheck, lint, or test commands, even to confirm something works. Judge whether tests prove the new behavior by reading the test files and the code they exercise together, the same way you already read the diff. If a test's assertions don't match what the change claims to do, that is itself the finding.

Do not run `entire review`, use other AI agents, or hand off the review. Do it yourself with the repo and local checks.

Rate the amount of **Slop** the change adds as Low, Medium, or Large. Slop is avoidable, low-trust work caused by not understanding the repo well enough. It creates extra bugs, review work, or maintenance work.

First understand what the change is trying to do. Follow every workflow, route, state change, and rule it touches from start to finish. Read whether the tests prove the new behavior instead of only matching the code or new text.

Base the rating on:

1. **Severity** — How much can the problem break or burden?
2. **Prevalence** — How much of the change has the problem?
3. **Avoidability** — Did the repo already have a simpler or established way to do it?

Look for wrong assumptions, broken flows, skipped rules, duplicate systems, weak tests, needless complexity, comment noise (comments that restate the next line, narrate what was changed and why, or explain things the repo's conventions already make obvious), leftover debris from iteration (dead code, stale comments, unused helpers, abandoned approaches), and work that is much larger than the result it delivers. Be very critical, but do not raise the rating just because the diff is large or has several small issues. Do not call necessary complexity slop, and do not charge the change for problems it merely sits next to.

Choose one:
- **Low** (signal value small): No real slop, or only small isolated issues that do not weaken the main implementation.
- **Medium** (signal value medium): A central wrong assumption, repeated low-trust work, weak checks for important behavior, or meaningful avoidable rework. The implementation can still be fixed without replacing its core.
- **Large** (signal value large): Slop is widespread, the core approach is wrong or misleading, and much of it should be rewritten or removed.

Report the rating as the signal. Its rationale must name the two strongest reasons for the rating, using concrete behavior or architecture problems, not surface-level signals. Report each concrete slop problem behind the rating as a finding anchored to the changed code it concerns.
```

### C. Publication on a Pull Request

* Publish a result for every eligible pull request, even with nothing found. To tag a finished Entire session as a review, `entire session attach <SESSION_ID> --review` (dry run first, `--force` only after the operator agrees, Section 4.C, Step 2.3).
* One inline thread per finding, anchored to the smallest changed range (≤ 10 lines) ([review comments API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments)); a file-level comment when no changed line fits; a pull-request-level comment with a stable identifier and exact file references when GitHub offers no valid target; never a finding only in hidden output and never an unrelated anchor.
* A pull-request-level summary for every eligible pull request with: the full base and head SHAs; Entire checkpoint intent coverage (when applicable) and the Slop Rating with its two strongest concrete reasons; checks executed, checks not executed, residual validation gaps.
* With no supported finding, the summary begins with exactly: `Review completed: no bugs, security defects, or other reportable issues were found in the reviewed changes, subject to the checks and residual validation gaps stated below.` — never silence, an emoji, an approval state, `LGTM`, or a claim about code outside the reviewed scope.
* Never secrets, credentials, unnecessary exploit payloads, or weaponization details in pull-request comments.

# Third-party components

This inventory covers every external GitHub Action invoked by the repository
workflows, the CI-only npm and browser validation tooling, and the externally
hosted components used by the profile or the Pages site. The repository's
package manifest contains only development tooling for browser-level
provenance tests. No npm package, browser binary, or FFmpeg binary is copied
into `site/` or the deployed GitHub Pages artifact; the site's committed
JavaScript uses browser built-ins and GitHub APIs.

The versioned inventory is the repository's **dependency graph** (Insights →
Dependency graph), which GitHub maintains from the committed manifest, lockfile
and workflow files and exports as an SBOM on request. Versions, version ranges
and immutable commit pins live only in `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and
the workflow files, where Dependabot updates them; this document deliberately
does not repeat them, so it can never drift from those sources. The official GitHub
Dependency Review action evaluates manifest and lockfile changes on every pull
request to `main`, and the Pages workflow installs the committed lockfile with lifecycle
scripts disabled.

The repository's original content is proprietary and all rights are reserved.
The licenses below apply only to their respective third-party components.

## GitHub Actions

requests.

This repository is **not versioned**: it publishes the personal profile of

version. Dates are written `DD/MM/AAAA` in Brasília time (UTC−03:00).

LCV Ideas & Software will triage reports privately, request clarification when needed, and coordinate remediation before public disclosure. Public disclosure should wait until a fix or mitigation is available, unless there is an immediate user-safety reason to do otherwise.

## Operational baseline

This repository follows the LCV Ideas & Software single-operator security baseline:

- GitHub secret scanning and push protection;
- Dependabot alerts and security updates;
- GitHub code scanning default setup for CodeQL;
- external GitHub Actions pinned by full commit SHA, as the repository's Actions policy requires;
- workflow-level `permissions: {}` with the least `GITHUB_TOKEN` grant required by each job;
- direct, SHA-pinned official Dependency Review, Zizmor, and OpenSSF Scorecard Actions. CodeQL default setup remains the native merge-protection signal; Zizmor and Scorecard publish SARIF for security visibility without repository-owned gates, baselines, wrappers, lockfiles, or workflow-contract validators;
- the official Zizmor Action does not yet expose `--strict-collection` ([upstream #141](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor-action/issues/141)), so collection syntax or schema errors can remain warnings. This accepted upstream limitation is tracked without adding a repository-owned executor or gate;
- external credentials assigned by purpose to protected environments restricted to `main`, with one
  documented exception: the Dependabot auto-merge workflow reads a fine-grained personal
  access token (Contents, Pull requests and Workflows, read and write) from the Dependabot secret
  `DEPENDABOT_AUTOMERGE_TOKEN`, because a workflow triggered by a Dependabot pull request can read
  Dependabot secrets only. GitHub does not inject these values automatically: an authorized job
  receives a secret only when its workflow explicitly references it. The auto-merge workflow runs
  only on Dependabot's own pull requests from this repository, grants no `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  permission, binds the arming request to the exact event head, fails visibly when the run carries no
  Dependabot secret (the secret is not configured, or the event was initiated by a person), and
  runs no Action, checkout, cache, artifact, or pull-request-controlled command. Fork and
  non-Dependabot pull requests never run it. The `Claude Code` workflow holds no credential: it
  authenticates by workload identity federation, as described under Automation policy;
- pull requests, squash-only merges, signed commits, linear history, resolved conversations, and required checks enforced by the repository's own rulesets, which mirror the organization's Enterprise rulesets because a personal repository inherits none of them;
- no long-lived secrets in source control.

### Personal-account product boundaries

GitHub secret scanning and push protection are enabled for this public repository. GitHub currently limits validity checks and generic/non-provider pattern scanning to eligible organization-owned repositories with GitHub Secret Protection; the corresponding settings therefore remain `PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE` for this user-owned repository. An API response that accepts an update without changing the readback is not treated as successful enablement.

### Contribution-snake provenance boundary

The profile's contribution snake is generated by the repository-owned, zero-dependency `scripts/generate-contribution-snake.mjs`. # Contributing

This personal profile repository is maintained by LCV Ideas & Software. Contributions should preserve the public profile, GitHub Pages, workflow, and security surfaces of `lcv-leo/lcv-leo`.

## Baseline

- Every change to `main` must use a pull request. Direct pushes, administrative merges, REST merges, force pushes, and ruleset bypasses are prohibited.
- Squash is the only merge method. A pull request is merged only after the effective repository rulesets and all required checks are satisfied on its exact head SHA. There is no merge queue; no workflow or operator may bypass the pull-request, signature, CodeQL, linear-history, or required-check gates.
- Do not commit secrets, tokens, private keys, credentials, generated build output, or local environment files.
- Set workflow-level permissions to `{}` and grant each job only the `GITHUB_TOKEN` capabilities it demonstrably needs. Keep privileged external credentials in protected environments and out of pull-request jobs. The documented exception is listed in `SECURITY.md`: the Dependabot secret `DEPENDABOT_AUTOMERGE_TOKEN`. The `Claude Code` workflow holds no credential; it authenticates by workload identity federation.
- Pin every external GitHub Action to an immutable commit SHA, as the repository's Actions policy requires; do not introduce a mutable reference.
- Preserve Dependabot checks every day, including weekends, at 05:00 in Brasília (`Etc/GMT+3`), automatic rebasing, and GitHub's post-merge branch deletion. The native cron schedule includes weekends; `daily` would check only weekdays. Every dependency is excluded from the cooldown (`*` inside each `package-ecosystem` block), so ordinary version updates are proposed immediately; the cooldown stays configured as a deliberate switch — replacing the `*` with narrower dependency-name patterns re-enables the delay for exactly what those patterns match. Security updates are grouped separately per ecosystem and run independently of that schedule and cooldown.
- Dependabot prepares dependency pull requests from this repository's own `.github/dependabot.yml`. The repository-local workflow `.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml` enables GitHub's native auto-merge on Dependabot's own pull requests; GitHub merges them only after this repository's rulesets and required checks pass. No external repository or custom controller operates their lifecycle.
- Do not add repository tests that assert a value Dependabot controls (Action commit SHAs, Action or package versions, lockfile contents) or that validate the shape of a workflow file: such a test inside a required check blocks automatic merging.
- Use `https://registry.npmjs.org/` by default. A different npm registry is allowed only through an intentional, versioned, applicable `.npmrc` rule.
- Do not change Enterprise or organization rules, settings, applications, or secrets without separate explicit operator consent.

## Validation

Before opening or updating a pull request, run the repository-specific checks documented in the README, package scripts, or workflow files. For security-sensitive changes, retain evidence of the checks performed in the associated Issue, Project item, Discussion, or pull request.

# Changelog — Oráculo Financeiro

## [Unreleased]

- Adota o lockfile de dependências de GitHub Actions
  (`.github/workflows/actions.lock`, gerado por `gh actions-lock --no-narrow`),
  que registra cada action em um commit exato junto com a identidade do
  repositório de origem e é atualizado pelo Dependabot no mesmo pull request.
  Todos os `uses:` dos workflows mantêm seu SHA completo e o comentário de
  versão; o lockfile acrescenta a pinagem das dependências transitivas que os
  arquivos de workflow não expressam. A política `Require lockfile` permanece
  desligada. Os consumidores customizados aposentados de `actions.lock` não são
  restaurados. Rastreio: LCV-719.

- O build, os testes e o desenvolvimento local geram os tipos do Cloudflare
  Pages e de cada Worker com o Wrangler do lockfile. O CI e o deploy conferem
  os três conjuntos de tipos em uma instalação limpa.

- Atualiza o Wrangler de 4.165.0 para 4.166.0 e regenera os tipos do runtime de Cloudflare Pages.

- Atualiza o Wrangler de 4.164.0 para 4.165.0 e regenera as declarações do
  Worker com Workerd 1.20261118.1. Sincroniza o lockfile e o inventário de
  terceiros (LCV-676).

- Atualiza as Actions oficiais Claude Code para v1.0.280 e Dependency Review
  para v5.0.1, com SHAs completos. A mudança da licença incorporada de minimatch
  para ISC foi autorizada pelo operador (LCV-666).
- Atualiza o Wrangler direto de 4.163.0 para 4.164.0, com lockfile regenerado
  pelo npm e tipos de bindings regenerados pela CLI oficial. Sincroniza as duas
  cópias do inventário de terceiros (LCV-666).

# Changelog

All material changes to the Android programme repository are recorded here.

## [Unreleased]

- Adopt the GitHub Actions workflow dependency lockfile
  (`.github/workflows/actions.lock`, generated by `gh actions-lock --no-narrow`),
  which records every action dependency at an exact commit together with the
  source repository identity, refreshed by Dependabot in the same pull request.
  Every workflow `uses:` reference keeps its full-length commit SHA and version
  comment unchanged; the lockfile adds pinning for the three transitive
  dependencies the workflow files cannot express (`oven-sh/setup-bun`,
  `actions/upload-artifact` v7.0.0 and `github/codeql-action` v4.39.3), recorded
  as transitive rows in `THIRDPARTY.md`. The `Require lockfile` policy stays
  off. This repository has no same-repository composite action, so neither
  `--migrate-local-actions` nor `--ignore-local-actions` applies. AGENTS.md and
  CLAUDE.md Sections 6.E item 2 and 7.A now copy the workspace master text that
  adopts the lockfile, replacing the passages that declared it nonexistent or
  retired, and the affected third-party inventory rows were aligned to the
  current workflow pins (LCV-719).
- Update Claude Code Action from v1.0.278 to v1.0.280 and Dependency Review
  Action from v5.0.0 to v5.0.1 at their full release commit SHAs, aligning
  the third-party inventory. Both Actions remain MIT-licensed; the operator
  explicitly accepted the Dependency Review bundle's minimatch notice

====
  only identifiers, no stored credential, and is not a required check.
- GitHub Pages deploys only the sanitized `site/` directory to the public page
  `https://programa-android.lcv.dev`; the page is deliberately excluded from
  search indexing.

Every external GitHub Action is pinned to a full commit SHA directly in its
workflow, and `.github/workflows/actions.lock`, generated by
`gh actions-lock --no-narrow` and refreshed by Dependabot in the same pull
request, additionally pins the transitive Action dependencies the workflow
files cannot express and records each source repository's identity
([Workflow dependency lockfiles](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles),
[Locking action dependencies](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/lock-workflow-dependencies)).
The third-party inventory is in [THIRDPARTY.md](THIRDPARTY.md).

# Third-Party Components

Scope of this inventory: every **direct** dependency declared by a manifest committed to this
repository, every GitHub Action invoked directly by the versioned workflows or by the starter
workflows in `workflow-templates/`, every third-party script loaded at runtime by a page this
repository publishes, and the third-party brand assets vendored by the published pages.

The versioned inventory is the repository's **dependency graph** (Insights → Dependency graph),
which GitHub maintains from the committed manifest, lockfile and workflow files and exports as an
SBOM on request. Versions, version ranges and immutable commit pins live only in
`package.json`, `package-lock.json`, the workflow files and `.github/workflows/actions.lock`, where
Dependabot updates them; this document deliberately does not repeat them, so it can never drift from
those sources. Transitive npm dependencies are pinned by the committed lockfile; the GitHub Actions
dependency lockfile (`actions.lock`, generated by `gh actions-lock --no-narrow`) additionally pins
the transitive Actions that no workflow file references and records each source repository's identity
([Workflow dependency lockfiles](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles)).
The official GitHub Dependency Review action
evaluates manifest and lockfile changes on every pull request to `main`, the Enterprise license-compliance
rule validates licenses, and the public-site workflows install the committed npm lockfile with
lifecycle scripts disabled and run npm signature and advisory checks. The repository intentionally
has no parallel scanner, pin auditor, containerized Zizmor runtime, or policy wrapper of its own.

Licenses below were read from each package's own published manifest or from its upstream
repository, not inferred.

| Component  | License           | Scope       | Source                                   |

# an image. The provenance gate blocks every external request by design, so this
# is the only check that can notice a card's host going dark.
name: Profile Media Liveness

  # touching only these files would run no workflow at all.
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

      - "scripts/check-readme-media-liveness.mjs"
      - "scripts/check-readme-media-liveness.test.mjs"
      - "scripts/pages-provenance-contract.mjs"
      - ".github/workflows/media-liveness.yml"
  schedule:
    - cron: "41 9 * * *" # daily, 06:41 in Brasília; after the Pages deploy of the day
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: media-liveness
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  probe:
    name: Probe embedded profile media
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

result.content:
Lock and verify GitHub Actions dependencies to protect your workflows
from supply chain attacks.

Actions are resolved by mutable tags and branches at runtime. This
extension pins every direct and transitive dependency to an immutable
commit SHA in a per-repo lockfile at .github/workflows/actions.lock,
so changes are visible in pull request diffs and tampered or hijacked
actions are caught before they run.

Scans all workflows under .github/workflows/ by default and fixes
what it can — pinning every resolvable action and updating the
lockfile. Pass --no-fix for a read-only check that writes nothing.

HOST AND AUTHENTICATION

Supported targets are github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data
residency (*.ghe.com). GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) is not supported.

In a tenant repository checkout, authenticate with
gh auth login --hostname TENANT.ghe.com, then run gh actions-lock.

Host selection: --hostname, then GH_HOST, then the current repository
(GH_REPO or a remote on a host known to gh), then github.com.
For github.com and *.ghe.com, GH_TOKEN takes precedence over GITHUB_TOKEN
and stored per-host credentials.
--hostname selects the host; it does not override token variables.

On *.ghe.com, actions from public github.com repositories are read with
GH_ACTIONS_LOCK_GITHUB_COM_TOKEN, else the login from
gh auth login --hostname github.com, else anonymously (60 requests/hour
per IP). GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN are never sent to github.com.

If an unintended token override causes authentication to fail, check
stored tenant credentials without exposing tokens:
  env -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh auth status --hostname TENANT.ghe.com

For setup and troubleshooting:
  https://github.com/github/gh-actions-lock#github-enterprise-cloud-with-data-residency

REF NARROWING

When a new workflow is first pinned and uses a partial version ref
like actions/checkout@v4, the lockfile narrows it to the highest
matching full semver tag (e.g. v4.2.1). Full semver tags are
effectively immutable — unlike major/minor splats, they almost never
move once published, so the pinned SHA stays valid longer between
lockfile refreshes.

Only freshly pinned refs are narrowed — already-locked deps are not
touched. Only refs that parse as semantic versions (v4, v3.2) are
candidates; branch names (main, canary) and non-version tags are
never narrowed because the latest semver release in a repo may have
nothing to do with the ref the workflow intended.
Pass --no-narrow to disable this behavior entirely.

--json selects the output format only (independent of --no-fix);
structured results go to stdout and progress to stderr:

  gh actions-lock --no-fix --json 2>/dev/null | jq .valid

ENVIRONMENT

GH_ACTIONS_LOCK_REPO_ROOT names the repository root instead of
searching parent directories for .git. Set it when relocking a
partial checkout without .git. $/ actions resolve against it, and
the directory must exist and contain the workflows.

GH_ACTIONS_LOCK_GITHUB_COM_TOKEN is a github.com token for reading
public github.com actions on *.ghe.com, for CI where there is no gh
login. A GHE.com job's GITHUB_TOKEN is issued by the tenant and doesn't
work on github.com. Use a fine-grained token with no permissions. It is
never sent to the tenant, or used when github.com is the selected host.

RUN LOGS

Every run except --verify-local saves its full --json output, plus the
repository and whether the run succeeded (with its error, if any), to
<user cache dir>/gh-actions-lock/logs/ (on macOS,
~/Library/Caches/gh-actions-lock/logs). Failed runs print the path.
Logs are kept for 14 days, up to 50. Attach the log to bug reports.

Usage:
  actions-lock [<workflow-path>...] [flags]

Examples:
# Verify all workflows and fix what's fixable
$ gh actions-lock

# Verify a specific workflow
$ gh actions-lock .github/workflows/ci.yml

# Read-only check for CI integration (writes nothing, exits 1 if invalid)
$ gh actions-lock --no-fix --json=valid,findings

# All fields as JSON
$ gh actions-lock --json


Flags:
      --accept-moved                               Re-resolve deps flagged as ref-moved or unreachable-pin to their current live SHA
  -A, --allow-all-runners                          Deprecated no-op: runner restrictions have been removed
      --allow-runners strings                      Deprecated no-op: runner restrictions have been removed
      --fail-on-warning                            With --verify, --verify-local or --no-fix, exit 1 when any warning is reported
  -h, --help                                       help for actions-lock
      --hostname string                            GitHub hostname to query (defaults to GH_HOST, current repo host, or github.com)
      --ignore-local-actions ./…                 Warn instead of failing when a local ./… action uses remote actions the lockfile can't cover
      --json fields[="valid,findings,workflows"]   Output JSON with the specified fields (valid,findings,workflows,dependencies,pins)
      --migrate-local-actions uses: ./…          Rewrite same-repo uses: ./… actions in workflows to the inherently-pinned `uses: $/…` form
      --no-fix                                     Read-only: report findings without modifying workflows or the lockfile
      --no-interactive                             Run without interactive prompts
      --no-narrow                                  Keep mutable version refs (e.g. v4) instead of narrowing to full semver (e.g. v4.2.1).
                                                   Only refs that parse as semantic versions are narrowed (v4, v4.2); branch names
                                                   like 'main' or non-version tags are never narrowed because a full semver tag is
                                                   far more likely to resolve to exactly one commit for its entire lifetime.
      --no-onboard                                 Refuse to onboard new workflows or actions; only re-pin already-tracked entries
      --profile dir                                Enable profiling: write trace, CPU profile, and HTTP log to dir
      --relock                                     Re-resolve every ref and advance moved ones (e.g. main, v4) to their current upstream SHA; leaves unreachable pins as errors
      --verify                                     Frozen check: run the same checks as the default without writing; fails if the lockfile is incomplete or the runner would reject a pin
      --verify-local                               Offline lockfile coverage check: verify every action ref has a lockfile entry.
                                                   No network calls, no authentication, no file writes — ideal for pre-commit hooks.
                                                   It does not check that the entries are trustworthy; use --verify in CI for that.
  -v, --version                                    version for actions-lock

below the table.

The versioned inventory is the repository's **dependency graph** (Insights →
Dependency graph), which GitHub maintains from the committed manifest, lockfile
and workflow files and exports as an SBOM on request. Versions, version ranges
and immutable commit pins live only in `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, the
workflow files and `.github/workflows/actions.lock`, where Dependabot updates
them. This document does not restate the direct pins, so it can never drift
from those sources; it records the exact commit of a transitive Action only
where the workflow files carry no `uses:` line for it. The GitHub Actions dependency lockfile
(`actions.lock`, generated by `gh actions-lock --no-narrow` and never edited by
hand) additionally pins the transitive Actions that no workflow file references
and records each source repository's identity
([Workflow dependency lockfiles](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles)).
The official GitHub
Dependency Review action evaluates manifest and lockfile changes on every pull
request to `main`, and the Pages workflow installs the committed lockfile with lifecycle
scripts disabled.

The repository's original content is proprietary and all rights are reserved.
The licenses below apply only to their respective third-party components.

## GitHub Actions

Every external Action pinned by a workflow `uses:` line is pinned to a
full-length immutable commit SHA with a version comment in the workflow files,
as the repository's Actions policy requires. `.github/workflows/actions.lock`,
generated by `gh actions-lock --no-narrow`, never edited by hand, and refreshed
by Dependabot in the same pull request, is the record of every resolved commit,
including the transitive Actions pulled in by those Actions, and of each source
repository's identity
([Workflow dependency lockfiles](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles)).
The table lists every external Action repository either pinned directly by a
`uses:` line or recorded by the lockfile; the row marked "Transitive only" has
no `uses:` line, and the subsection below names the exact commit of every
transitive dependency. Tooling that an
Action selects at runtime (the Linear CLI, the zizmor tool and Scorecard image,
and the CodeQL bundle used by code scanning) is governed by that Action's own
release and license; the Claude Code software itself has its own license, noted
below the table.

| Component                          | License                                                                      | Source                                              | Purpose                                                     |
